solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Skirt left among clothes

indicators.note: among says the abbreviation sits inside the word for clothes

parts.note: kit is a set of clothes, as in football kit

explanation.surface: A garment left lying among a pile of clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish knee-length pleated garment is a kind of skirt.

clue.text: Seafood keeping always hot …

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: fish is the general seafood
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: A seafood dish kept permanently warm, running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 3 Down, but each clue works on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Running a temperature makes a person hot, the sense of a fever.

clue.text: naughty boy takes one

parts.note: a scamp is a mischievous child
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Continuing from 2 Down, a mischievous child helps himself to one of the prawns.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Seafood' at the start of 2 Down, carried over by the ellipsis; 'takes' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaded langoustine tails served fried are a popular seafood dish.

clue.text: Perhaps scribble on an assortment of notes

parts.note: D, E and F are three musical notes, the first half of the mixed handful
A, C and E are three more musical notes, the rest of the mixed handful

explanation.surface: Doodling over a sheet of music, or a mixed handful of banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests banknotes or memos; here it means musical notes, and the six letters D, E, F, A, C, E are each one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Scribbling over something spoils its surface, and to spoil a surface by marking it is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Forget lines, and flee rehearsal

parts.note: an actor who dries forgets their lines
to run is to flee

explanation.surface: A panicking actor forgets the words and bolts from the rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'dry' is theatre slang for forgetting one's lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice run-through before the real event is a trial, a rehearsal.

clue.text: It's used in printing of revolutionary books

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned around, so the little word of is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A typeface used in printing radical political books.
explanation.definitionFit: A typeface, a set of characters of one design, is what a printer sets text in.

clue.text: One pulled from fire, in the old joke?

definitions.meaning: a nut roasted in the embers, as in pulling someone's nuts out of the fire

explanation.surface: Rescuing someone from a blaze, told so often it has become a tired anecdote.
explanation.definitionFit: Roasted nuts come out of the fire, and a hackneyed story is called by the same word.

clue.text: Reclines, flopping in part of car

indicators.note: flopping suggests falling about loosely, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sprawls lazily across the inside of a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: The muffler on an exhaust system that quietens the engine is one component of a vehicle.

clue.text: Bet he's from New England

definitions.meaning: a multiple wager on four selections, eleven bets in all
a native of the north-eastern US states

explanation.surface: A wager about a man's origins in the north-eastern United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a four-horse accumulator wager and the term for a New Englander.

clue.text: Flag raised initially in ship

indicators.note: in says the picked letter goes inside the word for a ship

parts.note: a steamer is a steamship

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of raised

explanation.surface: A flag hoisted aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow pennant flown from a mast is a kind of flag.

clue.text: Heard neckwear is Asian

indicators.note: heard means the word is what we hear, a sound-alike

parts.note: a tie is worn round the neck

explanation.surface: Someone reports that a necktie comes from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Thailand is a person of South-East Asia.

clue.text: I agree to try more than once

indicators.note: more than once says the word comes twice

parts.note: a judge hears a case, that is, tries it

explanation.surface: Someone concurs with a plan to keep attempting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' here is the courtroom sense: to hear a case.
explanation.definitionFit: The parliamentary cry of approval expresses agreement with a speaker.

clue.text: Confusing argon with tin is uneducated

indicators.note: confusing means mixing up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A student who mixes up two chemical elements shows a lack of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking knowledge or schooling is the meaning of the adjective.

clue.text: Gun shot big beast

indicators.note: shot means shattered or damaged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rifle bags a large animal on safari.
explanation.definitionFit: The wildebeest is a large African antelope.

clue.text: Corps joining battle in response to revolution

indicators.note: joining says the two pieces are put side by side

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
action is fighting, a battle

explanation.surface: An army unit enters the fray in response to an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Political opposition to radical change is reactionism; more broadly any response to something.

clue.text: Lacking energy, but worked in kitchen

definitions.meaning: cleaned the dishes after a meal

explanation.surface: A tired cook who nonetheless toiled in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both worn out and having done the dishes, its literal sense.

clue.text: To go over to the enemy is a fault

definitions.text: To go over to the enemy
definitions.meaning: to desert one's side, as a verb

explanation.surface: Changing sides in a war is a failing.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to switch allegiance; the noun means a flaw.

clue.text: Moan one's stuck in factory

indicators.note: stuck in says one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a plant is an industrial works
one's is one is, and I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A worker complains about being trapped in an industrial works.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintive complaint or lament, a literary word for a grievance.

clue.text: Aesthetic and robust? Not he

indicators.note: not he says the letters of the pronoun are dropped

parts.note: hearty means robust, vigorous

explanation.surface: Someone is cultured and burly, though apparently not a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy interest in artistic matters, sometimes pretentious, is an aesthetic leaning.

clue.text: A number of criminals, some getting angry

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Several crooks are losing their tempers.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of criminals working together is a mob of them.

clue.text: Insincere praise of coffee accepted by Cook

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside, so the coffee goes into the cooking word

parts.note: to fry is to cook
a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.surface: A cook is buttered up with compliments over a coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive compliments paid to win favour are exactly empty praise.

clue.text: Swindle run by a policeman

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
MP is a military policeman

explanation.surface: A con trick carried out by a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a racket or con is a fraudulent scheme.

clue.text: Caution: six-footer is full of hostility

indicators.note: is full of means the second piece is packed inside the first

parts.note: a bee, as an insect, has six legs
war is open hostility

explanation.surface: A warning that a very tall person is aggressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' looks like a tall person; it is an insect with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to caution someone is to warn them to take care.

clue.text: Study WW1 battle in first course

parts.note: to con is to study or learn
the Somme was a 1916 battle of the First World War

explanation.surface: A history student reads up on a famous battle in an introductory course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first course' sounds academic but is the opening course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear soup is typically served as the starter of a meal.

clue.text: Run into conflict in terror

indicators.note: into says the abbreviation goes inside the conflict word

parts.note: a fight is a conflict
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Someone flees into a battle in a state of panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden intense fear is terror.
